plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, the optimal action is straightforward: bid exactly my value of $30.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With no prior history to suggest collusion or unusual behavior, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do - you never benefit from bidding above or below your value. Bidding higher risks winning and overpaying relative to your value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $22, I should bid exactly $22 to maximize expected profit.
